title: Adopt Zero-Trust Security Architecture for Network Access
narrative: FEDC's current security model relies on network perimeter controls — VPNs, firewalls, and network segmentation — to protect internal systems. This model is increasingly inadequate given the growth of remote working, cloud-hosted services, and third-party system integrations. A compromise of the network perimeter grants broad access to internal systems. Several recent security assessments have identified lateral movement risk as a key vulnerability. We adopt a zero-trust security architecture. Trust is never granted implicitly based on network location. Every access request — from users, services, and devices — must be authenticated and authorised against defined policies. Micro-segmentation will replace broad network trust. Continuous verification will replace point-in-time authentication for sensitive systems.

requirements.title: Identity verification for all access
requirements.description: Every access request to internal systems must be authenticated using a verified identity, regardless of the network origin of the request. Network location must not confer any implicit trust.

requirements.title: Least privilege access
requirements.description: User and service accounts must be provisioned with the minimum access required for their defined function. Access rights must be reviewed and recertified quarterly.

requirements.title: Continuous session verification
requirements.description: Sessions accessing Confidential or Restricted systems must be subject to continuous risk evaluation. Sessions exhibiting anomalous behaviour must be challenged or terminated automatically.
